Use `enumerate()` in Python to loop over an iterable and have an automatic counter, avoiding manual index tracking.
Deep copy nested objects using Python's `copy.deepcopy()` to avoid side effects of mutating references.
In pandas, use `.loc` and `.iloc` for explicit label-based and integer-based indexing to prevent SettingWithCopy warnings.
Always set `random_state` (or `seed`) in machine learning pipelines to ensure experiment reproducibility.
When working with imbalanced classification datasets, consider using Stratified K-Fold cross-validation to maintain class distribution.
Gradient boosting models (like XGBoost, LightGBM) are highly sensitive to hyperparameter tuning; optimize learning rate first.
Feature scaling (e.g., StandardScaler) is crucial for distance-based algorithms like KNN, SVM, and gradient descent-based optimizers.
Use generator expressions instead of list comprehensions in Python when memory efficiency is critical for large datasets.
Prevent overfitting in neural networks using dropout layers, weight decay (L2 regularization), or early stopping.
When debugging a machine learning model, start by overfitting a tiny batch of data to verify the model can learn at all.
Use `is` for comparing identity (memory address) and `==` for comparing equality (value matching) in Python.
Use `.get()` with dictionaries in Python to provide a default value when a key may not exist, avoiding KeyError.
Use `with open(...)` context managers in Python to guarantee that files are closed properly, even if exceptions occur.
When evaluating regression models, Mean Absolute Error (MAE) is robust to outliers, while Mean Squared Error (MSE) penalizes them heavily.
Use Python list slicing `my_list[::-1]` as a fast and idiomatic way to reverse a list in-place/as a new copy.
Use `any()` and `all()` in Python to perform quick boolean evaluations across any iterable of conditions.
Pre-allocate memory for NumPy arrays or Pandas DataFrames instead of appending iteratively to greatly speed up code execution.
To handle categorical variables with high cardinality, consider target encoding or catboost encoding instead of one-hot encoding.
Regularly monitor your machine learning models for feature drift and concept drift in production to maintain accuracy.
In PyTorch, always call `model.eval()` before running inference to disable dropout and batch normalization behaviors.
